title: AI-enhanced surgical planning and possibly AI-designed skull implants in the Abu Dhabi separation of craniopagus twins Mercy and Goodness
summary: PureHealth/SKMC statement (5 Jun 2026) cites 'AI-enhanced surgical planning'; XRlabs' own release claims AI-designed implants. The twins were separated in four operations and returned to Nigeria.
account: The Abu Dhabi Media Office published PureHealth's statement on 5 June 2026 that Sheikh Khalifa Medical City (SKMC) had performed the GCC's first separation of craniopagus twins: Mercy and Goodness, born in Nigeria with 'heads joined at the top, fused skulls, and intertwined brain tissue and blood vessels', separated at 15 months in four procedures over six months by 'more than 60 doctors and clinicians from the UAE, UK, Brazil, and Nigeria', led by Professor Noor Ul Owase Jeelani of Gemini Untwined. The statement lists 'mixed reality-guided implant design and AI-enhanced surgical planning' among the methods, names no software, and says the skulls were reconstructed with custom 3D-printed titanium grafts and the twins were recovering well. The National and Khaleej Times (both 5 June 2026) report the same facts without the words AI or artificial intelligence. A CNN report carried by WKRC (22 June 2026) says the teams 'used artificial intelligence, mixed reality and virtual simulations to map out the procedures', that AI 'helped surgeons design custom skull implants and model how the girls' skin could be expanded', and that the four surgeries totaled over 40 hours across four months in 2025, with the twins since home in Nigeria. The only system-specific claim is XRlabs' own Business Wire release of 19 June 2026 (read via Medical Product Outsourcing), which says its platform let surgeons 'design implants within seconds' from CT data in mixed reality using an AI model 'trained on similarly aged infant head shapes'. The earlier verifier found no case report of these twins in Europe PMC and noted that the surgical group's 2026 Radiology paper on craniopagus imaging does not mention AI; this pass found none either. The date observed is the hospital announcement; the surgery dates are not published.
purpose: XRlabs says its platform is built to design patient-specific implants and plan operations in mixed reality; the hospital's 'AI-enhanced surgical planning' is described only generically. Implant design for this separation was the vendor's stated purpose.
system: XRlabs 'Surgical Intelligence' platform for AI-designed skull implants (identified only by the vendor) and unnamed 'AI-enhanced surgical planning' (PureHealth statement)
developer: XRlabs (implant design, per its own release); the hospital names no developer for the planning tools
deployer: PureHealth - SEHA Sheikh Khalifa Medical City, Abu Dhabi, with Gemini Untwined (Professor Noor Ul Owase Jeelani)
domain: Healthcare - pediatric neurosurgery and craniofacial surgery
segment: Craniopagus twin separation: surgical planning and patient-specific implants
taxonomy_note: No health category exists in the six types. The AI's claimed contribution is to the surgical team's planning and implant design (the vendor claims implants 'within seconds'; CNN reports the fastest separation among Gemini Untwined's nine cases), so organizational efficiency is the nearest fit; the benefit to the twins themselves is the separation. The AI role rests on the hospital's unnamed 'AI-enhanced surgical planning', one CNN report, and the vendor's own release; no clinical publication documents it.

ratings.reason: Two children joined at the head were separated, reconstructed and discharged home to Nigeria, per the hospital and press; the surgical team produced this outcome and no source quantifies the AI's share of it.
The vendor claims implant design 'within seconds' and CNN reports the fastest of nine Gemini Untwined separations, but no source gives planning time saved or a comparison without the AI.

ai_role.statement: The hospital's own statement credits 'AI-enhanced surgical planning' without naming a system; CNN says AI helped design the skull implants and model skin expansion; the earlier verifier read People/AOL as attributing AI vaguely to skin-expander timing. The only identification of a system is XRlabs' own release, which cites no clinical publication. The AI supported planning and implant design for a 60-person team; no counterfactual is given, and the separation itself was surgical work.

later.quote: Doctors reported the surgeries were successful, and the girls have since returned home to Nigeria after making a full recovery.
